To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

c-Myc activation selects for spontaneous inactivating mutations in the ARF-MDM2-p53 tumor-suppressor pathway, which is required to cancel the protective checkpoint function and accelerate lymphomagenesis in vivo.
the ARF-MDM2-p53 tumor suppression pathway is frequently inactivated in Myc-induced B-cell lymphomas.

c-Myc activates a p19(ARf)-Mdm2- p53 tumor suppressor program in primary mouse embryo fiboblasts and pre-B-cells that potentiates Myc-induced apoptosis and selects for immortalized cells with inactivated p53 or bialleic ARF loss.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of tumor formation, in this case the role of the ARF/Mdm2/p53 pathway in the development of lymphomas induced by the c-Myc protooncogene.
the role of the p53 tumor suppressor gene and its related genes in lymphoma formation.
the mechanisms of lymphomagenesis, and the development of lymphomas in Emu-muc transgenic mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ARF and p53 are important for tumor suppression in Emu-mcy transgenic mouse lymphomas.
ARF-Mdm-p53 pathway is the most important tumor suppressor pathway that is disrupted in Myc-induced B-cell lymphomagenesis in transgenic mice.
the ARF-MDM2-p53 pathway is an important tumor suppressor pathway and that the disruption of this pathway can lead to the formation of lymphoma in Emu-muc mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ARF and p53 are potent tumor suppressors in the Myc lymphoma model.
Myc activation strongly select for spontaneous inactivation the p53 pathway in vivo.
Myc activates the ARF-MDM2-p53 pathway, which in turn induces apoptosis in pre-B-cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tumor suppressor pathway mediated by p19(ARf), Mdm2, and p53 plays an important role in the control of c-Myc-induced lymphomagenessis in mice.
Myc activation strongly selected for inactivation of ARF and p53, which accelerated progression to malignancy.
the ARF-MDM2-p53 pathway plays a critical role in the prevention of Myc-induced lymphoma, and that the loss of ARF and/or MDM2 is an early and frequent event during the pathogenesis of this disease.
